settings.gas_constant_basis: Explicit SI numerical convention; source does not print the numerical R used in its regressions.

fit.objective: Minimize the maximum absolute log residual divided by each printed asymmetric log margin; energy slopes constrained to the source's reported marginal intervals. Source table re-calibration, not new experimental validation.

source.page_numbering: One-based PDF pages; printed pages 46,51,52 respectively.
source.source_scope: Thermal experiments in Chapter 2, no plasma. Same fixed, aged specimen and plateau conditions as the preceding source contract.

dry.locator: Figure 2.9, PDF page 51; dry experiment fit, not necessarily identical to extrapolated k2 in Table 2.1

wet.locator: Figure 2.10, PDF page 56; multiply by site density to obtain whole-specimen mol/s

adsorption.locator: Figure 2.11, PDF page 57; interpret log K as log(K_per_bar times 1 bar), not log of a dimensioned numerical quantity in Pa

known_source_qualifications: Text on printed page 52 says wet activation energy 180 +/- 14 kJ/mol, while Figure 2.10 and printed page 51 say 181 +/- 14; retain the graph-specific value and record the difference.
The printed prefactors and slopes are separately rounded and their covariance is unavailable; their marginal intervals must not be treated as independent confidence distributions.
The adsorption enthalpy is a proposed surface-path fit, not an independently measured calorimetric reaction heat or a complete intermediate thermodynamic state.
Source-rate observations and Table 2.1 were already used for fitting; leaving out one table row is an internal consistency exercise, not an independent real-world prediction.
No transient temperature program, CO2 inhibition law, active-area evolution or reverse-carbonation rate is provided by these relations.
source.redistribution: Only required numerical facts and locators are recorded; copyrighted PDF, page images and complete source scripts are not redistributed.

scope: Conditional temperature parameterization of source plateau tables. Calibration consistency and derivative arithmetic, not experimental transient qualification.
